research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of coverage from talent and role counts
structural influence role categories (usage x residual influence)
methodological_questions: Does lineup coverage vary within team-season beyond what role counts alone imply?
Is coverage separable from the number of role-holders on the floor and from a talent proxy, given that roles are defined from usage and residual influence?
What does it mean for the talent control to 'behave' (stable sign, no leakage, no outcome-derived construction, no collinearity blow-up)?
Are role assignments reliable across seasons or halves, and do they depend on outcomes?
Is the sample of 420,993 possessions and 90 team-seasons enough, given that stints are heavily clustered within team-seasons?
evidence_establishes: No historical evidence was available: retrieve_history returned an empty list, so no earlier study record bears on this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup role coverage has been measured or tested before
Whether role assignment is stable enough to define coverage
Whether any talent control has been tried, or how it behaved
Any effect size, variance component or power benchmark for this question
own_inferences: The glossary defines roles by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (influence beyond what usage predicts). Coverage is therefore partly mechanical. A median split fixes roughly half the rotation as high-usage, which caps how many organizers and terminals a lineup can hold. Counts and coverage are tied together by construction, and 'separable from counts' needs a permutation or count-matched null rather than a plain regression.

The question has three clauses (varies, separable, talent control behaves) with no thresholds, so it is not yet a falsifiable hypothesis. The design below supplies thresholds, and they should be frozen before analysis.

With three roles and five players, the chance of full coverage rises sharply with rotation depth and with the number of high-usage players. Coverage may be near-saturated in many stints, which would shrink the within-team variance.
Roles estimated and then evaluated on the same possessions give an overfit, circular coverage measure. Roles should come from separate data, such as a prior season or alternate games.

Any talent proxy built from results (plus-minus, net rating, BPM) is outcome-derived, and usage-based talent proxies overlap with the role definitions. Both threaten the claim that the talent control behaves.
The 90 team-seasons are probably 30 teams x 3 seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25), which leaves 2025-26 as a possible holdout. This is an inference from the count, not a recorded fact.
uncertainties: Exact role-assignment rule, rotation definition and residual-influence computation in this setting
Which talent measure is meant by 'talent control', and whether it is available in the per-game files
Distribution of lineup coverage and its stability across seasons
Whether 2025-26 data are in the 90 team-seasons
Share of possessions with an unclassified or missing initiator
Roster churn and trades splitting team-seasons

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned nothing, so the decision rests on the task statement, the glossary and my own reasoning. The proceed-with-changes decision and the probabilities are priors with no empirical support from earlier work.

blocking_constraints.text: Role definitions by median-split usage fix the role-holder count, so coverage is partly determined by counts. Only a count-conditional or permutation null can establish separability.
Separability and 'talent control behaves' are undefined until a talent measure and thresholds are fixed. Role stability across seasons and halves is unknown.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved. The glossary names the Structural Influence role categories, but no result relevant to lineup coverage was returned.

risks.text: Coverage is a function of how many organizers, shapers and terminals are on the floor. The raw coverage-versus-count association is a definitional floor, not a finding.

Talent, minutes, starter status, lineup role in the rotation and opponent strength all affect both who is on the floor and role labels. A talent proxy overlapping usage can absorb the signal or create collinearity.
Residual influence and usage come from the same possessions used for outcomes, and results-based talent proxies are outcome-derived. Both can build in circularity.
Roles or talent estimated on a season that includes the evaluated stints leak information. Estimate them out-of-sample, from the prior season or from games excluded from the evaluation.
There are only 90 team-seasons, while 420,993 possessions are clustered within them. Team-level inference has far fewer effective observations than the possession count suggests.
Many five-man units have few possessions, and low-coverage lineups may be rare or confined to garbage time or bench minutes.
Role labels depend on a rule-based play-type classifier and its inferrer. They may be unstable for low-minute players and may change with the cutoff.
Roster changes, trades, injuries and league-wide style change across 2022-26 can shift role distributions between seasons and between regular season and playoffs.
Several definitions of coverage, talent control and subsets (RS vs PO, season) invite forking paths.
Stint reconstruction from substitution data and initiator linkage may mis-assign players or drop possessions.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified quantities. (1) Within-team share of variance in stint-level full-coverage (>=1 organizer, >=1 shaper, >=1 terminal among the five on court), from a team-season random-effects model. (2) Excess coverage dispersion: observed within-team coverage variance versus a null that permutes role labels among the team's rotation players, which holds role counts fixed. (3) Talent-control behaviour: change in the coverage coefficient or variance share when a pre-registered, out-of-sample, non-outcome talent proxy is added, plus the stability and sign of the proxy.
design.unit: Five-man stints (same ten players on court) nested in team-season; inference clustered at team-season. Possessions are used only as weights.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 RS and PO (90 team-seasons as recorded) for development. 2025-26 RS and PO form a locked holdout, used once, if the pipeline is frozen first. Exclude garbage time, and require a minimum stint possession count (set before analysis, e.g. >=10) and rotation membership by minutes. Report RS and PO separately and do not pool them.
design.power: Not computable from retrieved evidence. Before any outcome analysis, run a simulation using the observed role-count distribution. Planted within-team coverage effects should be detectable with at least 80% power at team-season-clustered N=90. Otherwise the test is declared underpowered and reported as inconclusive, not as null. Report the design effect from clustering.
design.controls: (a) The number of organizers, shapers and terminals on court, and minutes-weighted rotation depth. (b) A talent proxy built from the prior season or from games disjoint from the evaluated stints, preferring non-outcome measures such as minutes share or box-score rates, with outcome-derived proxies run only as sensitivity. (c) Starter status and opponent strength. Roles are assigned from a different season or different games than the stints scored. Check collinearity (VIF) between the talent proxy and usage-based role definitions. Report role-assignment reliability, such as split-half or season-to-season agreement.
design.falsification: Permutation placebo: shuffle role labels within team-season among rotation players, preserving counts, to build the null for coverage dispersion. Random-stint placebo: assign pseudo-lineups with the same count distribution. A negative-control talent proxy (random noise, or a proxy from an unrelated season) should neither remove nor create separability. Separability is rejected if the observed within-team coverage variance falls within the permutation null (two-sided 95%), or if the coverage effect drops by more than a pre-set fraction (e.g. 50%) after count control. Talent control 'behaves' only if its sign and magnitude are stable across the three seasons and the VIF stays below 5.
design.multiplicity: Three primary tests (variance share, excess dispersion vs permutation null, talent-control stability), with Holm correction at family alpha 0.05. Threshold choices, rotation cutoffs and minimum-possession cutoffs are fixed before looking at outcomes. Alternative definitions are labelled exploratory and reported in full.
design.decision_rule: Supported if: within-team variance share of coverage is at least 0.20 (a threshold to be fixed at registration), observed dispersion exceeds the permutation null after Holm correction, the effect survives count and talent control with at most the pre-set attenuation, the talent control passes stability and VIF checks, and the holdout direction replicates. Rejected if the powered test finds near-zero within-team variation or full permutation-null equivalence. Untestable or inconclusive if role reliability is below the registered floor or the simulated power is under 80%. Any apparent effect that disappears under the permutation null is reported as an artifact of the count mechanics.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type possession graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26. 2025-26 RS is complete from 2026-04-13 and PO from 2026-06-21. Freeze the extraction date, classifier version, role rule and analysis code (hash) before analysis. Record row counts (420,993 possessions, 90 team-seasons) and verify them against the frozen snapshot.

methodological_questions: Does lineup role coverage vary within team enough to be tested, beyond between-team differences?
Is role coverage separable from talent and from the number of role players on the floor (collinearity, mechanical dependence)?
Does the talent control behave as expected (stable, non-leaking, not outcome-derived)?

TOOL_RESULT glossary:
# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.

- **Possession, PPP:** a team's continuous spell with the ball; PPP is points per possession.
- **H1, H2:** first half (periods 1 and 2) and second half (periods 3 and 4) of a game. RS and PO: regular season and playoffs.
- **Play type:** the label assigned to each possession by the project's rule-based classifier from play-by-play events. Labels include PNR (pick-and-roll ball handler), DRIVE, CUT, SPOT_UP, PULL_UP, POST_UP, PUTBACK and TRANSITION. A play-type mix is a team's share of possessions in each play type.
- **Initiator, initiation:** the offensive player whose action starts the possession's play type (for example the cutter on a cut, the ball handler on a pick-and-roll). Initiation records are possession-level rows linking initiator, play type and points.
- **Inferrer:** the classifier step that infers a play type (for example a pick-and-roll) from play-by-play text when it is not recorded directly.
- **Suppression trigger:** a team, play type and game in which the team's PPP on that play type falls sharply from H1 to H2 under fixed minimum-attempt rules; read as the defense possibly taking the action away.
- **Continuation, counter:** after a trigger, continuation means the offense keeps running the triggered play type; a counter is a different play type run instead.
- **BEST, AVOID (counter tiers):** the strategy app's matchup-ranked counter recommendations after a trigger. BEST is the top-ranked counter play type for that matchup, AVOID the lowest-ranked.
- **Structural fingerprint:** a team's standardized pattern of how play types share initiators.
- **Structural influence (load, L):** how much a team's structural fingerprint changes when one player's initiations are removed. L_pre is that quantity measured from games before an absence.
- **Usage:** a player's share of team possessions he initiates or finishes.
- **Role categories (Structural Influence paper):** by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (structural influence beyond what usage predicts): Primary Organizer (high usage, positive residual), Shaper (low usage, positive residual), Terminal Scorer (high usage, residual at or below zero), Role Occupant or Specialist (low usage, residual at or below zero).
- **Connector:** a structural-role label used in later studies for players whose presence links teammates' play types; the exact rule varied between studies.
- **Hub:** a high-structural-influence player around whom a team's initiations are organized.
- **Absence spell:** a run of consecutive games a player misses (the main studies used at least 15).
- **Displacement (D_real):** how far teammates' play-type mix moves during an absence spell relative to before it (one minus the cosine similarity of the two mixes).
- **Mover, decoy:** a mover is a player who changed teams between seasons; decoys are comparison players used as placebo matches for a mover.
- **Stint:** an interval of play with the same ten players on the court.
- **Garbage time:** late-game possessions with a lopsided score, usually excluded.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm checking whether my role categories are sound: they come from usage and play-type patterns, and usage is tied to initiations and finishing, so role coverage is mechanically linked to counts. "Talent control" is still undefined, and splitting roles at the rotation median would make about half of every team look high-usage by construction.

I'm now settling the design: roles would be assigned from a prior-season or out-of-sample split so the coverage measure isn't leaking outcome information, and I'd test three things, the within-team share of coverage, its separability after controlling for role counts and talent, and whether the talent control stays stable without absorbing coverage.

I'm settling the data window: fixing 2022-23 through 2024-25 for development, with 2025-26 held out, though the 90 team-seasons suggest 2025-26 may not be in the count. Next I'm setting up a permutation null that shuffles role labels within each team-season, to see what coverage looks like once counts are held fixed, and I'll compare that against the observed dispersion. Three primary tests will go under a Holm correction.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm checking whether my role categories are sound: they come from usage and play-type patterns, and usage is tied to initiations and finishing, so role coverage is mechanically linked to counts. "Talent control" is still undefined, and splitting roles at the rotation median would make about half of every team look high-usage by construction.

I'm now settling the design: roles would be assigned from a prior-season or out-of-sample split so the coverage measure isn't leaking outcome information, and I'd test three things, the within-team share of coverage, its separability after controlling for role counts and talent, and whether the talent control stays stable without absorbing coverage.

I'm settling the data window: fixing 2022-23 through 2024-25 for development, with 2025-26 held out, though the 90 team-seasons suggest 2025-26 may not be in the count. Next I'm setting up a permutation null that shuffles role labels within each team-season, to see what coverage looks like once counts are held fixed, and I'll compare that against the observed dispersion. Three primary tests will go under a Holm correction.
